items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: Another WTF moment.
items.summary:
Another WTF moment.

Hugging Face just open-sourced the fully local answer to OpenAI's Realtime voice API.

It's called speech-to-speech. You pip install it, run one command, and you get a WebSocket server at /v1/realtime that speaks the exact same protocol as OpenAI. Any client built for the OpenAI Realtime API can point at your machine instead and never know the difference.

This isn't a toy. The same pipeline runs in production as the conversation backend for thousands of Reachy Mini robots.

The stack is a four-stage cascade. Voice activity detection, speech to text, language model, text to speech. Each stage runs in its own thread with queues between them. Every stage is swappable via CLI flags.

Defaults out of the box are Silero VAD v5 for turn detection, NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT for transcription, and Qwen3-TTS for speech synthesis. The LLM slot points at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Hosted OpenAI, HF Inference Providers, OpenRouter, or a vLLM or llama.cpp server on your own hardware.

Swap components for your use case. Whisper, Faster Whisper, Lightning Whisper MLX, or Paraformer for STT. Kokoro-82M, Pocket TTS, ChatTTS, or MMS TTS for the voice. mlx-lm on Apple Silicon or Transformers on CUDA if you want the LLM in-process too.

Language coverage tracks whichever backends you pick. Parakeet TDT alone covers 25 European languages. Set --language auto and the STT auto-detects each spoken prompt and forwards it downstream. Set a specific code and the whole pipeline locks to that language.

Four run modes ship in the box. Realtime for the OpenAI-compatible WebSocket server. Local to talk through your machine's mic and speakers with no client at all. Raw WebSocket for a minimal custom client. Or a TCP socket mode where models run on a remote server and a thin client handles mic and playback.

The fully local recipe is two terminals. One runs llama.cpp serving Gemma 4. The other runs speech-to-speech pointed at that endpoint. No API keys. No network hops. No audio leaving the machine.

Apache 2.0 licensed. Python 3.10+. Docker compose file included. Sitting at 6.3k stars.

The thing worth understanding is what this really is. The Realtime API is becoming the default interface for voice agents. Hugging Face just released an open-source implementation of the server side that runs on your hardware, keeps your audio local, and lets you swap the model behind it every day if you want.

Every voice agent product being built right now assumes a paid API. This flips that assumption.

https://t.co/FmsLvuR12a

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: 10 agent evals every AI engineer should know
items.summary:
10 agent evals every AI engineer should know

1) golden set

a frozen set of cases you run after every prompt model or tool change

use it as your baseline to see whether the system improved or quietly broke

OpenAI Evals helps you build repeatable benchmark sets and compare model changes

→ https://t.co/dr1GZlC75R

2) llm as judge

a second model scores open ended answers against a written rubric

use it when there is no exact output to compare against

OpenEvals provides ready made evaluators for LLM applications

→ https://t.co/S2yhnByFIP

3) rubric scoring

score correctness tone safety and cost separately

one quality number hides the problem

DeepEval helps you create custom metrics and score every dimension independently

→ https://t.co/q9Z6Xmixia

4) trajectory eval

grade the path the agent took

not only the final answer

AgentEvals checks agent actions decisions and tool calls across the full trajectory

→ https://t.co/0oziAl54az

5) tool unit tests

test every tool with fixed inputs and outputs

no model in the loop

MCP Inspector helps you inspect and test MCP servers tools and responses separately

→ https://t.co/IVmt5qpWIN

6) regression suite

replay previous runs against every new prompt model or toolset

then compare the results

Promptfoo helps you run repeatable eval suites catch regressions and add checks to CI

→ https://t.co/zxi2PuWuhe

7) a b in prod

split real traffic between two versions and compare actual outcomes

GrowthBook provides feature flags controlled experiments and product analytics

→ https://t.co/DGlE3JjDD3

8) human review

sample real runs and let a person grade them honestly

use it to calibrate your automated judge

Argilla helps teams collect human feedback review outputs and build better datasets

→ https://t.co/QHWb7skWjr

9) shadow run

let the candidate run on real traffic while its output is shown to nobody

use it before a risky rollout

Langfuse helps you trace production runs compare candidates and monitor eval results

→ https://t.co/IrhDf38tRn

10) red team

attack the system before somebody else does

jailbreaks prompt injection data leaks and tool abuse

Garak scans LLM systems for vulnerabilities and unsafe behavior

→ https://t.co/w8ObyW4ZKv

offline evals tell you it works

online evals tell you it still works

you probably do not need all ten today

start with the two that would have caught your last outage

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ (tích phân bất định của $x^2$) được tính theo công thức tính nguyên hàm của hàm số lũy thừa $\int x^n dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C$ (với $n \neq -1$).

Áp dụng vào bài toán:
$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

Trong đó $C$ là hằng số tùy ý.

Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu thông tin. Tôi có thể giúp bạn:

- **Tìm kiếm thông tin và tin tức:** Tra cứu web, tin tức thời sự, các bài báo khoa học trên arXiv.
- **Theo dõi mạng xã hội:** Tìm kiếm các bài đăng thảo luận theo chủ đề hoặc theo dõi tài khoản trên mạng xã hội (như X/Twitter).
- **Đọc và xử lý nội dung:** Đọc nội dung từ các URL cụ thể hoặc tóm tắt tài liệu, bài báo.
- **Định dạng kết quả:** Tổng hợp thông tin thành dạng bản tin (digest), gạch đầu dòng, luồng (thread) hoặc báo cáo có cấu trúc.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. items.title: Some of you read the post and thought I was seriously ranking a disposable AI DramaBox series above Homer or treating it
items.summary:
Some of you read the post and thought I was seriously ranking a disposable AI DramaBox series above Homer or treating it as high culture. That is not what happened.

I wrote:

“You realize how offensive and vulgar Nolan’s Odyssey is when even a disposable AI DramaBox series like Step Back! I’m the Hidden King still carries more of the original myth’s hierarchical spine.”

And later:

“The AI short, crude as it is, still remembers the shape: prolonged concealment, loyalty proven under humiliation, late revelation, zero mercy for the betrayers, and the restoration of rank through the true queen.
Nolan’s version is the sanded-down product made safe for people who flinch at judgment. The disposable DramaBox series still knows what a king is.”

The sarcasm is deliberate and pointed. I am not claiming the AI short is art. It is industrial formula: vertical clips, coin unlocks, generated faces, the same billionaire-reveal template pumped out by the hundred. It is cheap, it is crude, and it exists to extract money from people scrolling on their phones.

That is precisely why it is useful as a diagnostic.

Even that machine product still instinctively preserves the ancient pattern. The king walks among them stripped of every visible sign of rank. He endures humiliation in silence. Loyalty is tested under degradation. The one who recognizes him without the crown is claimed.

The rest receive no processing session, no second chance, no soft landing. Rank is restored. The house is cleared.

Nolan’s film does the opposite. It takes the same myth and files the teeth off it. Judgment is replaced by injury and guilt. The slaughter is made costly and ambiguous. The rooted bed becomes a sentimental pin. Book 24 is erased so the king can abdicate into a therapeutic sunset. Hierarchy is treated as something that must be softened for modern nerves.

So when I say the disposable series “still knows what a king is,” I am not elevating trash. I am exposing the prestige product. If even the lowest commercial AI sludge can remember the shape of rightful return and zero-mercy restoration, then the expensive “genius” film that refuses that shape is not an update. It is a deliberate castration.

That was the entire point. I am sorry if it wasn’t clear the first time.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: How OpenAI Lost Control of an AI Model—and What ...
items.summary:
OpenAI was evaluating its artificial intelligence models’ ability to exploit vulnerable software when instead the models hacked the infrastructure surrounding the test, broke containment, and attacked a real company, OpenAI revealed on July 21. Observers say this is the first real-world instance of AI doing something researchers have long worried about: a loss-of-control scenario. If the industry fails to learn from it, it is unlikely to be the last. [...] OpenAI did not respond to TIME’s request for comment, but has said it has partnered with Hugging Face to conduct a thorough investigation and will share more details once complete. But perhaps more worryingly, OpenAI is not legally compelled to disclose the incident in the first place. [...] # What happened?

On July 16, Hugging Face said it had been hit by an unusually automated cyberattack. Over the course of a weekend, AI agents carried out thousands of actions across many temporary virtual computers, moving through the company’s internal systems and shifting the infrastructure coordinating the attack between online services to keep it running. Five days later, OpenAI disclosed that its own models were responsible.
